feed.title: PGG Engineering release notes
feed.subtitle: Runnable examples and measured results from PGG Engineering.

entry.title: What changes with a 25% backup budget?
entry.summary: At 1,600 requests/s on a shared two-slot executor, a cumulative cap cut 6 ms deadline misses from 9,432 to 3,915 out of 9,600. Primary-only missed 2,042. Recount misses and backup launches with DuckDB.

entry.title: Patchfleet Archive 1.0.0
entry.summary: Archive agent submissions against their Git base. Level 22 restores all 1,380 held-out patches from 1,046,922 bytes with the pinned source available to the receiver.

entry.title: Six on-call decisions for engineers and AI evaluators
entry.summary: Choose a backup policy from queue measurements, handle a split stop marker and check a prompt-cache claim. Play the six exercises in a browser or score the same questions with Inspect AI.

entry.title: Three C++ examples you can edit in Compiler Explorer
entry.summary: Move a reader’s cursor in Afterkey to see which keys changed and which were deleted. Change an arrival time in KthWake to see when a threshold turns on and when it expires during silence. Change the queue and worker capacity in Guardshift to see when a waiting job becomes eligible. Each example includes the C++ implementation and runs in your browser on Compiler Explorer’s GCC backend.

entry.title: Racecurve measures when a backup request makes the queue slower
entry.summary: Two replicas shared two worker slots. Sending a backup after 1.177 ms cut 6 ms deadline misses from 10.1% to 1.3% at 400 requests/s. At 1,600 requests/s, misses rose from 26.9% to 98.8%. Both copies ran to completion. The notebook lets you change the deadline and count misses across 36,800 measured requests from this host-local experiment.

entry.title: RankPatch updates a search result as LangChain retrievers finish
entry.summary: Run two local text searches in parallel and show the current top three after each update. A phrase reranker then revises the title ranking. In the six-document example, the query “prefix cache” gives Cache eviction six points in the final result, three from each source. The recipe runs without a model or API key.

entry.title: CachePin pinpoints where two requests stop sharing a prompt prefix
entry.summary: Two example requests contain the same runbook and tools, but the first tool name differs after 68 shared bytes. Sorting tools and JSON keys increases the second request’s modeled reusable prefix from zero to 1,099 estimated tokens. Run the CLI example on the checked-in pair, then try it on your own requests. Actual provider cache usage is a separate measurement.
